strengths: Correctly assigned the cluster to the macrophage lineage from observed markers (MARCO, MSR1, C1QA, FCAR, TFEC, ACP5, TREM2).
Recognized alveolar/activated/interstitial alternatives in its top-k.
weaknesses: Remained at the ancestor level and did not refine to the supported alveolar macrophage subtype.
Top-2 combined label is not a single ontology-valid cell type.

strengths: Correctly identified macrophage as the dominant lineage.
Listed alveolar macrophage as the second candidate, consistent with MARCO/MSR1 marker evidence.
weaknesses: Primary label stayed at the general macrophage ancestor despite direct marker support for the alveolar descendant.

strengths: Selected the most specific ontology-valid descendant with direct positive support (MARCO, MSR1, C1QA, TREM2, MS4A4A, MS4A14, TFEC, ACP5, FCAR, SNX10).
Aligned with lung alveolar macrophage identity while excluding T/NK/neutrophil alternatives.
weaknesses: Reported enrichment p-values were non-meaningful, so marker interpretation rather than pathway statistics carries the decision.

supporting: Original DEGs contain classic alveolar macrophage markers MARCO, MSR1, C1QA, FCAR, TREM2, MS4A4A, MS4A14, TFEC, ACP5, and SNX10.
Reactome enrichment for Innate Immune System and Scavenging by Class A Receptors supports the scavenger macrophage phenotype.
PMID 39560475 provides interpretable literature context for lung macrophage marker-based annotation.
conflicting: TREM2 can also mark lipid-associated/activated macrophages, but this is best interpreted as an activation/state component, not a separate lineage.
Enrichment p-values were flagged as unreliable, but marker-level evidence remains decisive.
enrichment_or_literature: Binding and Uptake of Ligands by Scavenger Receptors
